subject: Recap: VectorCare evaluation — hyperscaler risk matrix + dedicated asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@vectorcare.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@vectorcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: VectorCare evaluation — hyperscaler risk matrix + dedicated asks

Jordan / Priya — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick written recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

TL;DR: VectorCare is evaluating production inference options for clinical summarization (low 10s qps steady, spikes to ~600 qps during overnight batch ingestion). Primary concerns are capacity guarantees during spikes, multi-region failover, and PII handling for auditability. You asked for a side-by-side of Redwood Dedicated vs. CloudScale reserved GPUs and a short recommended test matrix.

Key notes from the call:
- Workload profile: steady ~8-15 qps during day; big nightly window (01:00–05:00 UTC) with 400–600 qps sustained for 20–40 minutes.
- Latency target: p50 < 50ms token latency, p95 < 220ms for 2k token summaries.
- Data requirements: logs retained for 90 days, search audit trail required for HIPAA-aligned SOC2+/BAA workflows.
- Risk factors you highlighted: hyperscaler preemption during peak autoscale, pricing unpredictability with egress, and procurement preference for reserved contracts.

What Redwood will provide next by Wednesday (attached):
1) A short risk matrix comparing Dedicated (reserved pool) vs. CloudScale reserved instances vs. CloudScale on-demand (PDF attached).
2) A pragmatic test matrix we recommend for qualification (latency, tail, saturation, failover, and cost per token).
3) A sample SLA and outage/fallback playbook for Dedicated capacity.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
- VectorCare to share sample payloads for a 24-hour window and an expected spike schedule. (Action: VectorCare)
- Redwood to run a focused test: 2k-token model, scale to 700 qps sustained for 30m on Dedicated and CloudScale reserved configuration. Deliverables: latency/tail, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost delta. (Action: Redwood, owner: Marissa)
- Procurement check: VectorCare to confirm preferred contract cadence (monthly vs. 12/24-month reserve). (Action: VectorCare)

I attached the draft risk matrix and the test matrix CSV so we can lock the test plan quickly. If that looks right, we can schedule the test window the week of Nov 9 and you'll have numbers to present to procurement.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-risk-matrix-v1.pdf, requested-test-matrix.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: VectorCare evaluation — hyperscaler risk matrix + dedicated asks

Adding technical detail and a slightly stronger test suggestion.

Jonas — good notes. A couple of clarifications from engineering: we should run two variants of the spike test to capture queueing and KV-cache warmup behavior:
- Variant A (cold KV cache): spin up new instances, load the model, drive to 700 qps for 30m; measure initial 10 minutes separately for warmup behavior.
- Variant B (steady-state warm cache): pre-warm KV cache and start from a warmed state to measure steady tail latency.

Metrics to capture (minimum): p50/p90/p95 latency per token, 99th percentile inference latency (end-to-end), GPU utilization, memory pressure, batch size distribution, and token throughput per second. Also capture the number of dropped or throttled requests and queue sizes.

On the Dedicated configuration we propose to reserve a heterogeneous pool (mix of A100-like and L40s-like instances) so we can test both cost-optimized and latency-optimized paths. We'll include a short cost delta estimate versus a single-instance reserved approach.

I attached an internal CloudScale latency file we've used as a baseline for comparison (cloudscale-latency-report.xlsx). Jordan — if you can provide a sample 24-hour payload and clarify the overnight window start time (local), we can finalize the dates.

Marissa
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: VectorCare evaluation — hyperscaler risk matrix + dedicated asks

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from VectorCare side before we lock a window: 

1) Procurement prefers 12-month reserved if the cost delta is <12% vs. on-demand. We will need a simple TCO comparison.
2) For the 24-hour sample payload: attaching a sanitized snippet (see attached) — main surge starts ~02:15 UTC local (on most nights) and lasts ~30–35 minutes.
3) A concern from our infra team: what protections do you provide for multi-region failover (if an entire AZ/hyperscaler region has capacity pressure)? Would Dedicated be able to failover fast without double-billing?

If Redwood can demonstrate: (A) an internal failover test (switch routing to a second region with <60s disruption), and (B) clear cost differential for reserved vs. reserved-on-hyperscaler, procurement will be comfortable moving to a 12-month committed path.

Jordan Lee
Director, Platform Engineering | VectorCare
jordan.lee@vectorcare.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: VectorCare evaluation — hyperscaler risk matrix + dedicated asks

Jordan — great, thanks for the sample payload and procurement guidance. Confirming what we'll deliver and owners for the week of Nov 9: 

1) Risk matrix v1 (Jonas) — includes AZ/region failure modes and mitigation notes for Dedicated vs. CloudScale reserved. Expect PDF with short summary and recommendation.
2) Two-run test plan + schedule (Marissa) — Variant A (cold) and Variant B (warmed). We'll include a short playbook to execute an inter-region failover test that simulates AZ loss; objective is <60s disruption with auto-routing to backup pool.
3) TCO snapshot (Karthik & Neha) — 12-month reserved vs. hyperscaler reserved vs. on-demand. We'll show cost per 1M tokens baseline and delta percentages for your finance/procurement review.

We propose the test window on Nov 11–12 (UTC friendly) — Marissa, Karthik: can we lock Nov 11 for Variant A and Nov 12 for Variant B? Jordan / Priya: please confirm if those dates work and whether you want Redwood to run tests in your VPC (we have a Private deployment option) or in our Hosted/Dedicated lab.

Once you confirm, we'll send a short execution checklist and calendar invites.

Thanks — Jonas
